current_abi_answer.layout_distinction: A separately reviewed Rust-owned owner/sidecar can potentially keep existing C structure sizes unchanged. That still introduces a NEW defined kind/ref/closing/group-membership protocol and interfaces; it is not an existing pin in the present ABI. No such record/token/interface is implemented here.
current_abi_answer.reason: It can serialize a short list lookup/mutation only while held. Current APIs return raw pointers after unlock, provide no transferable event pin, and permit close to free the event. A persistent event.group_leader pointer outlives any short lookup lock.

existing_event_pin_or_refcount.count_is_not_a_refcount: mc_perf_event.count is ihk_atomic64_t explicitly commented counter_value, with child_counter_value separately recorded. It is hardware measurement state, not an ownership token.
existing_event_pin_or_refcount.opt_is_not_a_free_existing_owner_slot: mckfd.opt is void* with no perf owner semantics in the participating publisher; publisher does not initialize opt or dup_cb. It cannot be silently reinterpreted as an established typed owner.
existing_event_pin_or_refcount.raw_links_are_not_pins: group_leader/parent and list membership do not stop perf_close_body_result from freeing the event.
existing_event_pin_or_refcount.real_mc_perf_event_fields: attr/extra_reg/hardware configuration, measurement count, child_count_total, pmc_status, sample_freq, raw parent/group_leader links, sibling/group lists, counters/timestamps/hardware fields; no lifetime refcount or closing/pin token.
existing_event_pin_or_refcount.real_mckfd_fields: next,fd,sig_no,data,opt,read_cb,ioctl_cb,mmap_cb,close_cb,fcntl_cb,dup_cb; no reference count, closing state or kind field.

first_missing_contract.close_participation: The actual perf_close_body_result invokes free(event); the group helper has no ownership edge excluding concurrent close. The entry final-publication lock_fn/unlock_fn applies later and does not guard this lookup/mutation.
first_missing_contract.exact_approved_replacement_provider_name: UNKNOWN / not supplied by current entry or helper; this review does not invent one.
first_missing_contract.exact_field: matching proc.mckfd entry: mckfd_data_offset / real Mckfd.data: CLong
existing_signature_lacks: descriptor-kind/callback identity predicate or actual matching-field offset
group/list reservation ownership or compatible lookup/teardown lock callbacks
observed_behavior: Walks proc.mckfd via raw next/fd/data offsets without an acquired lookup lock.
Treats data as an event pointer solely because fd equals group_fd; no descriptor-kind or expected callback check occurs.
Writes event.group_leader then leader sibling/group links, nr_siblings and pmc_status without a retained event reference or group reservation.
first_missing_contract.required_existing_provider_contract: A reviewed genuine provider must establish that this exact group_fd owns a live perf event, retain the descriptor/event and serialize group membership through success and all failure/close paths. No such provider is passed or consumed by this actual helper.
first_missing_contract.restriction: Forwarding group_fd unchanged into this unsupported pointer/lifetime contract would enter the excluded undefined/ownership domain. Restricting to group_fd=-1 would reduce original supported scope, so no such projection is prepared.
first_missing_contract.why_necessarily_reached: A valid supported sys_perf_event_open request may specify an existing group_fd. Current validation does not establish descriptor type/lifetime, and the complete body calls this helper unconditionally before host-FD request.

first_missing_existing_interface: No current provider has the contract: resolve group_fd to a verified live perf owner under lookup exclusion and retain/release it across group mutation, host-FD work, publication failure and close/teardown. Exact approved prototype is absent; this review invents none.

lock_participation.participation: No mckfd lock acquisition and no lock callback in signature. Non-standalone branch follows raw proc.mckfd and uses fd match then data as event; writes leader/group lists and counters.
Event/counter allocation and group mutation happen before host-FD callback. lock_fn/unlock_fn are passed onward only to final descriptor publication, not used to protect earlier group resolution.

Initializes fd/sig_no/data/read/ioctl/mmap/close/fcntl fields before taking process mckfd_lock. Lock protects insertion at head; unlock occurs before return. It does not acquire a group/event lifetime ref.
Takes mckfd_lock, finds raw descriptor, unlocks, returns pointer; no pin/reference is acquired. Its name does not mean returned storage stays locked.

Takes mckfd_lock, unlinks descriptor and clears next, UNLOCKS, invokes descriptor close_cb, frees descriptor, then forwards Linux close. Thus lookup lock released before callback cannot prevent event/desriptor destruction.
Reads event from sfd.data, clears current thread counter allocation maps, then directly free(event). No event reference release/defer protocol or group-member unlink/reparent is performed here.

On final VM path, process mckfd_lock is HELD while calling every close_cb. close_all neither unlinks entries nor acquires event refs; descriptor nodes are freed by later process drain. A new close callback that blindly reacquires mckfd_lock would self-deadlock on this path.
Existing IRQ-save ticket spinlock and paired IRQ/preemption restoration. It is not a blocking reference lease and must not be held across the host-FD do_syscall transaction.
